$comment: S5 judge rubric (methodology/05-eval-rubric.md #judge). exam-examiner, 2026-08-16, round 1. Dimensions: 1 single-defensible-best-answer, 2 distractor-plausibility, 3 concept-alignment, 4 rationale-traceability, 5 difficulty-pitch, 6 scenario-realism. Every distractor was argued FOR before scoring; 'case' records the strongest distractor case per item and why it loses (full method + bank-level findings in derivation/eval-report.md). Dimension-5 policy this round: score = min(content pitch, surface-cue score), where the surface cue is the keyed option's length/comprehensiveness asymmetry (keyed-option length as % of the longest distractor, 'r' below): r>=150 -> 2 (the surface hands the answer over), 125-149 -> 3, 110-124 -> 4, <110 -> no cap. The cue is real: the examiner's own 67/67 blind solve and the fact that the keyed option is the longest in 51/57 SC items make the bank solvable by test-wiseness alone. See bank_defects for the two systemic records (key position, option shape) that accompany the per-item bounces.

items.case: B (DL as umbrella) is a real learner confusion argued at full strength, but inverts containment on the concept's own terms; C's supersession claim echoes market hype yet is flatly false; D's 'one AI label' is a heard-in-meetings cop-out. Key stands. r=141 caps dim5.

B (algorithm=model renamed) is the strongest: teams do speak loosely this way; it loses because the procedure exists independently of the artifact it produced. C (seeing data = learning) and D (self-improving in production) are genuine practitioner misconceptions.

D (price bands) is defensible product pragmatism - bands do simplify reporting - but discards the continuous output the stem requires; B's cluster-average is a real naive approach that wastes the labels; C's RL framing has no environment to learn from.

D (async inference with callbacks) has a genuinely strong case - overnight completion fits the timeline - and loses only on operational load: per-record submission rebuilds a batch job from queue parts. B/C/D are all real serving modes from distinct patterns; best distractor set of its kind in the bank. r=137 caps dim5.

B (rows-and-columns = tabular) is the strong case - most engineers would say it - and loses because temporal ordering is a property of the data, not the container; D's schema-confers-structure is a subtler real confusion; C is weaker (no practitioner truly merges the feeds).

C (no GPU cluster) is the best wrong pick: a real feasibility-review finding; it loses because compute is rentable and says nothing about task fit. D (vendor demo errors) is anecdote-as-measurement; E's blanket PII prohibition is a false claim a cautious reviewer might half-believe.

D (classification into risk bands) is the strongest: classification IS an application category and rostering could use buckets; it loses because the roster needs a quantity. B's fraud framing trades on the word 'false'; C is over-engineering with a real-world echo. Keyed option is the SHORTEST here (r=81) - the counter-cue this bank needs more of.

SM. The live confusion is Transcribe/Polly direction (s1,s2,s5) and Comprehend-vs-Translate on s4 ('convert...into other languages' reads superficially like Comprehend's text work). Option reuse (Transcribe twice) defeats one-to-one elimination. Clean key.

B (upload after flight) is a real architecture that loses only on the in-flight requirement; C (GPU ground vehicle) is an inventive real workaround defeated by cost/ops; D's fine-tuning-gives-explainability is the exam's target misconception. Three strong distractors from distinct patterns. r=131 caps dim5.

Ordering-as-SC. B (features before cleaning) is the plausible slip for anyone who learned 'feature engineering first'; C's evaluate-in-prod is a real startup habit; D is correct except for dropping monitoring - the best near-miss. Key not longest (r=81).

C (spend the grant collecting data) is the strongest: 1,200 photos IS small for scratch training - the premise is true, the conclusion wrong because adaptation doesn't need scratch-scale data. B fails on resources; D's deferral is realistic grant behavior but produces nothing. r=132 caps dim5.

D (runbook by the departing engineer) has a genuinely good case - documentation is standard offboarding and any director would order it; it loses because it documents an unrepeatable process rather than instituting a repeatable one. B (buy a platform) and C (shadow hire) are equally real responses. r=135 caps dim5.

B (recalibrate threshold) is the strong tempter: thresholds ARE legitimately tuned post-launch; it loses because it moves reported rates, not scores' correctness for the drifted population. C (weights degrade) is a pure D19 giveaway; D (bigger model) is a real instinct. r=139 caps dim5.

C is the model half of the key plus a plausible-sounding business measure - the survey's lag and population mismatch are what a candidate must see; B is the classic accuracy-at-2%-base-rate trap; D's one-number F1 tempts real dashboards. Options length-balanced (r=100), key not first-by-length. The bank's benchmark item alongside 5.08.

B (1:1 word-token) is a stated false claim but exactly what a non-LLM engineer assumes; C (characters) is its sibling; D (wait for invoices) is real finance behavior yet eliminable without the scenario. r=139 caps dim5.

B (embed whole filings) has the strongest case in the item - long-context retrieval is a live practice debate - and loses on the stem's own requirement (find passages, not filings). C's topic tree is a real alternative architecture; D's bigger-chunks-carry-more is a genuine tuning misconception. r=137 caps dim5.

C (context engineering) is a near-co-correct label - worked examples ARE context in the colloquial sense - and loses because the team edited instruction/example text itself, the defining prompt-engineering act, and the question's point is that no training cost exists. B's 'lightweight fine-tuning' is the director's own confusion made into an option. r=132 caps dim5.

SM. s5 (style variants of an existing image) carries a defensible second reading - modern image-editing models take image+text instruction and could be called multi-modal; 'diffusion' wins as the canonical family for image generation/variation, but the rationale does not address the s5 ambiguity (dim4 4). s3 is the intended multi-modal discriminator and works well.

B (archive OCR as GenAI) is genuinely instructive - candidates must see that exact fidelity is anti-generative; C (churn scorer) rightly tests GenAI-vs-classical-ML. D (impress the board) is eliminable without reading the scenario - one throwaway option weakens the set (dim2 3). r=132 caps dim5.

Ordering-as-SC. D (stops at deployment, no feedback) is the best near-miss - correct sequence, truncated loop; B swaps evaluation for live feedback, a real move; C's tune-then-pretrain inversion is detectably wrong to anyone with the concept. Key not longest (r=95).

Content is the bank at its best: B (distill) fixes cost but not throttling; C (cap output) trims the small side of a 6000/400 split; D (re-index) touches neither mechanism - each distractor is a real, single-lever mistake. But the keyed option is a 179%-length dual-clause essay that argues both levers with 'rather than' hedging: the surface hands it over. Bounced on shape, not substance.

B (prompt engineering) is the strongest neighbor - sharper wording feels like the fix and loses only because wording cannot fetch a record that was never assembled; D (bigger window) is the real-world default response and loses on prioritization-still-undefined. Thin-flag concept (C-022) holds up well.

MR. C (larger context window) is the strongest wrong pick - 'agentic behavior emerges with enough context' is a live claim in the field; it loses because capacity confers neither action nor persistence. D (timeout) and E (fine-tuned weights required for tool use) are distinct real confusions. Thin-flag C-023 holds.

D (keep one agent, sectioned mega-prompt) is a genuinely defensible engineering position in current practice - it loses on this stem because the errors already cross sections, which is the evidence the patterns address; B's load-balancer reading is the naming trap. Thin-flag C-024 holds.

C (pack tool docs into context) is the best distractor: it describes what teams actually did before MCP and loses on imitation-vs-invocation; B invents an AgentCore scheduling role (E01); D's transport-standard reading trades on 'protocol'. Definitional item, wardrobe light. Thin-flag C-025: accurate to the v1.1 blueprint. r=132 caps dim5.

B (corrupted artifact) is the engineering-lead instinct made concrete and loses because coherent well-formed fabrication is not corruption's signature. C (disclose) and D (users verify) are both eliminable as bad practice without engaging the scenario - dim2 3. r=134 caps dim5.

C (temperature zero) is the strongest distractor in the bank: most engineers believe it guarantees identity, and in practice it often nearly does; it loses because no configuration promises it and the broken design assumption survives. B (retry until agree) and D (runbook waiver) are real ops behavior. r=134 caps dim5.

B (leaderboard) is the intended trap and a real selection habit; C (cost-only) is defensible procurement discipline that loses on constraint violation; D (partnership pricing) is real but eliminable. Keyed option restates the whole constraint-filter doctrine at r=150 - surface cue bounces it.

B (SageMaker AI) is the strong near-neighbor - it CAN host FMs - and loses on the no-infrastructure requirement; C (agent-first with Strands) mirrors real 2025-26 hype; D (self-host for independence) is a real preference argued as a requirement.

MR. D (full control of weights) is the strongest wrong option - it IS an advantage, just of the opposite stack; the sides-swap is a fair discrimination. C's hallucination-elimination claim is the target false belief; E's prompt-text access rules is a wrong-layer confusion tested again at 5.01C - acceptable, different domain.

C (multi-modal because radiology) is the clever trap - the workload is dictated text, imaging happens upstream; B (parameter count as proxy) is a real heuristic that loses on limits; D (vendor bundle) is real procurement behavior but eliminable without the scenario's specifics.

Excellent distractor set: D (provisioned throughput) is the RIGHT answer to the neighboring problem (2.07) placed here as a wrong one - genuine cross-item discrimination; B (fine-tune the rules in) loses updatability; C (trim detail) trades fidelity. Thin-flag C-032 holds on substance. But r=152 with a because-clause essay key - bounced on shape.

B (switch top-k to top-p) is the strongest: it names real sibling parameters and loses because neither supersedes the other nor undoes widened randomness; C (fine-tune for consistency) mistakes knowledge for sampling; D is detect-not-fix.

B (quarterly fine-tuning) is the canonical wrong answer argued at strength - it loses on cost cadence and staleness windows; C (stuff the library into every prompt) is the real brute-force move; D (system-prompt-only grounding) is what many teams actually ship. Content strong; r=200 (key is a double-length architecture lecture) - bounced on shape.

B (DynamoDB holds arrays) is the strongest - factually true storage claim that loses on search-by-similarity being the job; D (model dictates store) is a real coupling misconception; C (recompute on demand) is weak but real for tiny corpora. r=142 caps dim5.

B (RAG cheaper than ICL) has a defensible real-world case at scale (long prompts recur per-call; retrieval amortizes) - it loses on the blueprint's canonical implementation-cost ladder, which the item explicitly invokes ('implementation cost and effort'). C's tuning-first habit and D's pretrain-first are distinct real behaviors. Key not longest within noise (r=110).

B (agent = bigger model) is the one strong distractor - a real conflation; C (zero oversight) and D (cost per conversation) are eliminable without the scenario (dim2 3). Keyed option enumerates book/update/notify with a 'rather than' hedge at r=157 - the definitional content plus the shape cue make this the most surface-solvable item in d3. Bounced.

C (post-generation moderation pass) is nearly co-best in real practice - an output filter IS the robust control for banned phrasings; it loses only because the stem asks how a working prompt is built and C leaves the prompt broken. That framing dependency is worth the Gate 2 read (dim1 4). B (repeat the instruction thrice) and D (recency positioning) are real prompt folklore. r=147 caps dim5.

SM. s4 (stored prompt with placeholders) is simultaneously zero-shot in example count - 'prompt template' is the best label because reuse is the defining property described, but a candidate reading by example-count has a defensible s4=zero-shot case (dim1 4). s1/s5 double zero-shot exercises option reuse well.

B (hijacking) is the strong near-neighbor and the argued-FOR case is real - the assistant now serves attacker content; it loses because the assistant still performs its own task and the corruption lives in the corpus (the taxonomy's own discriminator). C (hosting intrusion) misreads the attack; D (moderation will catch it) is deferral.

C (shared change log) is versioning's manual ancestor and a defensible interim control - it loses on skipped entries, drift, and no-rollback, but the gap is operational rather than categorical (dim1 4). B (single gatekeeper) and D (weekly regression tests) are real partial responses. Thin-flag C-041 holds. r=132 caps dim5.

B (fine-tuning) is the strong neighbor defeated by the unlabeled corpus + all-tasks goal; C (pretrain from scratch) is the maximalist instinct; D (distill now) inverts the sequence and the stem plants the kiosk hook fairly. Content good; r=163 with the key naming method+reason+later-plan - bounced on shape.

B (swap instruction-tuning/domain-adaptation labels) is the fair naming trap; C swaps transfer learning for continuous pre-training - the subtlest wrong option, defeated because no further unlabeled training is described; D's 'all preference alignment' collapse is eliminable. Key NOT longest (r=83) - proof the author can write counter-cue items.

MR. C (maximum volume) is the strongest wrong option - 'more data beats better data' is a real belief defeated by scale-multiplies-defects; D (30-day recency) dresses a schedule as quality; E (raw authenticity = no curator bias) is a subtle real position defeated by curation being a stated requirement.

B (SFT on correct responses) is the one strong distractor, defeated by the stem's no-labeled-answer premise; C (raise temperature for warmth) and D (train the users) are eliminable without the scenario (dim2 3). Keyed option restates RLHF's definition plus the no-label rationale at r=155 - bounced.

B (public benchmarks) is the strong objective-sounding wrong answer - defeated because no benchmark measures this audience's persuasion standard; C (complaints as channel) is real passive practice; D (prompt author reviews own output) is D20 made into an option - nice touch. r=174 essay key - bounced on shape.

C (BERTScore, similarity implies faithfulness) is the strongest - a modern-sounding metric with a subtle false implication; B (BLEU as universal standard) is the planted engineer's claim; D is opinion sampling. The two-part ask (right metric AND what it cannot tell you) pitches this well.

C (re-index more often) is the strongest wrong move - a plausible cause adopted without localization; B (bigger benchmark samples) re-measures a settled question; D is a disclaimer-not-fix. Thin-flag C-048 holds; the compose-fallacy content is exactly the blueprint's application-evaluation objective.

MR. C (ROUGE vs approved library) is the strong tempter - a scalable number on the wrong question; D (leaderboard) tests model-vs-application again fairly; E (annual brand survey) is a lagging confounded signal a board might actually cite.

MR. C (fairness emerges from volume) is the strongest wrong belief and the rationale kills it cleanly; D (single-market uniformity for label consistency) has a defensible-sounding premise defeated by vanishing populations; E (post-deploy complaint channel) is detective-for-preventative.

C (system-prompt instruction) is the strongest - it is what most teams ship first, defeated by request-vs-enforcement; B (fine-tune the topics out) is the planted engineer's proposal; D (canned menus) achieves policy by deleting the product - real but eliminable.

C (offsets) is the strongest distractor - actual corporate practice with a real accounting logic, defeated because selection avoids the consumption offsetting merely neutralizes; B's efficiency-resolves-it misstates proportional scaling; D defers. r=138 caps dim5.

B (boilerplate covers it) is the strong legal-adjacent distractor defeated by generated-content being outside its precondition; C (swap in operational risks) is real risk-register behavior. D (keep it low-profile) is concealment eliminable without the scenario (dim2 3). r=140 caps dim5.

B (underfitting) is the intended discrimination and fairly argued; C (re-draw the validation split) is real p-hacking behavior; D (camera noise) is defeated by the stem's validation-images control - well-constructed evidence. Content solid; r=172 diagnosis-plus-consequence essay key - bounced on shape.

C (drift monitoring) is the strongest near-neighbor in d4 - a monitoring answer to a fairness question, defeated because since-launch unevenness shows no drift; B (fresh aggregate) re-measures the concealing number - the exact mechanism the concept teaches; D (transparency report) is disclosure-not-discovery. r=148 caps dim5.

B (documentation satisfies both) is the strong conflation the concept exists to break; C (seek exemption) is refuse-the-mandate; D (decline-letter notice) is the thinnest-slice answer. Content is a clean property distinction; r=154 both-properties key - bounced on shape.

B (KMS + CloudTrail) is the strongest - a fully-audited model feels explained, and the security-vs-explainability swap is a real conflation; C (trust page) is PR-as-artifact; D (wait for open source) is deferral. r=172 four-artifact enumeration key - bounced on shape.

C (ensemble + post-hoc explainer) is a genuinely defensible modern practice (surrogate/attribution methods are used in regulated settings); it loses on the stem's defend-every-decision strictness, but the rationale's 'defending fiction' overstates - post-hoc XAI is not categorically fiction (dim1 4, Gate 2 read). B's accuracy-is-safety is the target dogma; D routes the decision away from the accountable owner. r=143 caps dim5.

D (CloudTrail first) is the strongest - logging IS a first-day control in real rollouts, defeated by detection-vs-prevention on the 'first control' ask; C (prompt-text access rules) is the wrong-layer confusion; B (shared service account) is real integration expedience. r=134 caps dim5.

MR. C (quarterly access review) is the strongest wrong control - a real governance practice on the wrong requirement (detection, not protection); D (privacy notice) is paperwork; E (broaden access to simplify encryption) has a superficially operational logic defeated by blast radius.

B (train then output-guardrail) is the strongest - guardrails exist and the sequence error is the tested concept; C (Inspector) is the service-role swap a checklist-reader makes; D (vendor NDA) is paper-around-data. r=144 caps dim5.

B (same checklist everywhere) is the target habit, fairly argued; D (duties end at network) is a real narrow reading of shared responsibility; C (settle at procurement) is real but eliminable. Content aligned to thin-flag C-062 and correct - but r=214, the worst shape offender in the bank: the key is a 3-clause doctrine statement against three one-liners. Bounced.

B (input-side screening suffices) is the strong wrong boundary - defeated because model-originated leakage needs no harmful prompt; C (retrain until incapable) is the weights fallacy; D (weekly transcript review) fails never-emit by cadence. Thin-flag C-063 holds on substance; r=155 three-control enumeration key - bounced on shape.

B (fine-tune to refuse injections) is the strongest - adversarial training is a real research direction, defeated because the model's judgment is the attacked surface; C (pre-read produced documents) is a real manual control that scales poorly; D (encrypt the repository) protects integrity, not content semantics. r=153 - bounced on shape.

B (model version records account for outputs) is the strongest conflation - versioning feels like provenance; defeated by nondeterminism and context dependence. D (30-day purge) is a real data-minimization instinct colliding with provability; C (client survey) is the slowest signal.

B (Config timeline) and C (CloudWatch metrics) are both strong: each answers a genuinely adjacent question and a candidate must know the discriminator (configuration state vs aggregate counts vs per-call identity); D tests shared-responsibility ownership of the record. Key is SHORTER than two distractors (r=90). With 1.14, the shape model the rework should copy.

B (rewrite the binder) is the strong near-fix - a fresher document feels like the audit response, defeated because operation, not text, lapsed; C (buy a compliance suite) is tooling-for-practice; D (freeze and defer) converts obligation into acknowledged non-compliance. r=163 lifecycle-lecture key - bounced on shape.

bounces.judge_case: Keyed option argues BOTH levers (trim prompts + provisioned throughput) with a 'rather than a model-quality problem' hedge at 179% of the longest distractor's length, while B/C/D are each single-clause single-lever claims. A test-wise candidate picks the comprehensive both-sides option without knowing GenAI cost mechanics. Distractor content itself is excellent (see items case).
bounces.required_fix: Rewrite the keyed option to parallel shape with the distractors (target <=120% of the longest distractor, one clause, no self-justifying 'since/rather than' rider - move the argument into the rationale, where it already lives). Alternatively raise B/C/D to argued two-clause form. Do not change the key's semantics or the tested concept. Rebalance the key letter away from A while editing (bank_defects BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Keyed option restates the entire constraint-filter doctrine (all three constraints + 'no single score decides') at 150% length; distractors are one-liners. The doctrine-restatement style makes the key identifiable as 'the textbook sentence' without engaging the airline scenario.
bounces.required_fix: State the key as a decision ('Filter on the three binding constraints, then choose the most capable survivor') without the appended rationale clause; keep distractors as-is. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key explains prompt caching's mechanism AND why it fits ('precisely because so many requests share the same leading context') at 152%; the same information already appears in the rationale. D (provisioned throughput, correct for 2.07's problem) deserves a fair fight and the shape denies it one.
bounces.required_fix: Trim the key to the action ('Enable prompt caching so the repeated preamble is reused as a cached prefix'); drop the because-clause. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key names RAG, the grounding mechanism, an AWS product example, and the why-retraining-fails argument in one 200%-length option. Any candidate selecting 'the option with the embedded example and justification' scores without knowing RAG.
bounces.required_fix: Reduce to 'Retrieval Augmented Generation, grounding each answer in guidance notes and bulletins retrieved at question time' - the Bedrock Knowledge Bases mention and the since-clause belong in the rationale (already there). Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Two compounding weaknesses: the key is a 157%-length definition with example enumeration and a 'rather than' contrast, and two of three distractors (C zero-oversight, D cost-per-conversation) are eliminable without engaging the scenario, leaving B as the only working distractor. Surface + thin set = no real discrimination.
bounces.required_fix: Shorten the key to the coordinator-of-actions claim without the example list; replace C or D with a distractor from a distinct live pattern (e.g., agent-as-RAG-retrieval confusion, or agent-requires-fine-tuned-model per 2.09E but differently framed). Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key names the method, the reason it fits, and the correct placement of distillation later - three moves in one 163%-length option against three single-move distractors. The 'with X reserved for later' rider is a stylistic key-marker throughout this bank.
bounces.required_fix: End the key after 'extending domain knowledge across tasks'; the distillation-later contrast lives in the rationale. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key restates RLHF's definition plus the exists-precisely-for-this justification at 155%; C (temperature for warmth) and D (train the users) are eliminable without the scenario, so B is the only live distractor and the shape gives even B's fight away.
bounces.required_fix: Trim the key to the technique + one clause; strengthen C or D into a genuinely tempting option (e.g., best-of-n sampling with user ratings as a filter, or DPO/preference-tuning named incorrectly as supervised fine-tuning). Rebalance key letter (BD-1).
bounces.note_3s: dimension 2 at 3 recorded for the Gate 2 read of the reworked item

bounces.judge_case: Key chains human-in-the-loop -> calibration -> LLM-as-judge -> the AWS product in a 174%-length pipeline sentence. Distractors are single practices. The candidate needs only to spot 'the option describing a whole workflow'.
bounces.required_fix: Split the load: key states the pairing ('human evaluation on a sample to set the standard, LLM-as-a-judge calibrated to it for scale'); drop the Bedrock Model Evaluation rider to the rationale. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key delivers diagnosis + mechanism + the subgroup observation at 172% while each distractor is one alternative diagnosis. The stem's evidence design (validation-set control) is good; the option shape spends it.
bounces.required_fix: Key = 'The model is overfitting - it memorized training specifics rather than the general pattern'; move the unevenness observation to the rationale. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key defines both properties AND assigns each request its artifact at 154%; B/C/D each make one move. The both-properties-in-one-option shape is the reliable key-marker.
bounces.required_fix: Key = 'These are different properties needing different artifacts: transparency covers the system, explainability covers the individual decision'; trim the definitional expansion. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key enumerates four artifact families (Model Cards, Clarify, OSS disclosure, human-centered feedback) at 172%; distractors name one thing each. Enumeration-vs-single-item is instantly visible.
bounces.required_fix: Either trim the key to two load-bearing artifacts (Model Cards + Clarify) matching distractor granularity, or make B a plausible enumeration too (e.g., 'IAM roles, KMS encryption, CloudTrail, Config' - four security controls, same shape, wrong property). Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Worst shape offender in the bank (214%): the key walks through the shared-responsibility model, names the Scoping Matrix, and lists the three duty families that shift, against three one-line distractors. The item is unmissable without any AWS knowledge. Substance (thin-flag C-062) is otherwise correct and well-aligned.
bounces.required_fix: Key = 'The split of duties depends on how much of the GenAI stack you own; the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix maps the shift from consuming SaaS to building on a platform.' Duty enumeration moves to the rationale. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key maps each requirement clause to its named control (leakage prevention / toxicity filtering / hallucination detection via grounding + confidence) at 155% - a three-for-three enumeration against single-note distractors.
bounces.required_fix: Key = 'On the output side: filtering and validation of what leaves the model before any user sees it.' Control-by-control mapping moves to the rationale. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key names the attack AND the full counter-architecture (data-vs-instruction segregation + capability scoping) at 153%; B/C/D each offer one wrong counter. Naming-plus-counter in one option is the key-marker.
bounces.required_fix: Split: 'Prompt injection: untrusted document text carried instructions the model obeyed; the counter sits at the input boundary, treating third-party content as data.' Drop the capability-limitation rider to the rationale. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bounces.judge_case: Key restates the operated-lifecycle doctrine with the full obligation list at 163%; the three distractors are each a one-line partial response. The audit-finding stem is strong; the option shape answers itself.
bounces.required_fix: Key = 'Governance was treated as a document instead of an operated lifecycle - policies, review cadence, and training never ran after launch.' Trim the obligation enumeration. Rebalance key letter (BD-1).

bank_defects.finding: The keyed answer occupies the first position(s) in 67/67 items: all 57 single_choice keys are 'A', all 7 multiple_response keys are exactly ['A','B'], and in all 3 scenario_matching items the first N scenarios map to matching_options in listed order (1.08 s1-s4 = options 1-4; 2.04 s1-s3 = options 1-3; 3.09 s1-s4 = options 1-4). The player (apps/web/components/question-card.tsx) renders options via Object.entries insertion order with no shuffle, so this is the on-screen order as shipped: a candidate who notices scores 100% with zero knowledge, and every distractor_patterns map tags only B/C/D (or C/D/E), which leaks the key to any tooling that displays metadata.
bank_defects.required_fix: Author-side: rebalance key letters across items to an approximately uniform distribution per domain (mechanical permutation of option letters + answer + distractor_patterns keys + rationale.distractors keys; no content changes needed), and vary MR key pairs and SM scenario-option correspondence. Engine-side (routed to Oliver/tech-manager, not the author): a seeded render-shuffle in the player would make JSON order immaterial and is worth having regardless - but data-level balance is still required because exports, print forms, and third-party renderers see JSON order.
bank_defects.ratchet_proposal: Add a validator check: chi-square or max-share bound on key-letter distribution per exam (e.g., no letter keys more than 40% of SC items; MR pairs not constant; flag distractor_patterns maps whose key set never includes the answer letter as a key-leak).

bank_defects.finding: The keyed option is the longest option in 51/57 single_choice items; median keyed-option length is 134% of the longest distractor, and 15 items are at >=150%. The keyed option is also stylistically marked: it is routinely the only option with a both-sides construction ('X, since Y rather than Z'), an embedded justification clause, or a multi-control enumeration, while distractors are single-note claims. The longest-most-hedged-option heuristic solves the bank without domain knowledge. The distillation itself warned about this (derivation/source-declute-serverside.md: 'authoring must keep option shapes parallel within an item') - the warning did not make it into the authored bank.
bank_defects.required_fix: Bank-wide rework wave: for every item with keyed length >=125% of the longest distractor, either trim the key's justification riders (the argument belongs in rationale.correct, where it already exists nearly verbatim) or raise distractors to argued parity. The 15 >=150% items are bounced individually (entries above); the 22 items at 125-149% are dimension-5 3s in the Gate 2 sample and should be swept in the same wave. Models to copy: 1.14, 5.08, 3.13, 1.07 (keys at or below distractor length, all six dimensions 4-5).
bank_defects.ratchet_proposal: Add a validator check: keyed-option length must be <=125% (warn) / <=150% (error) of the longest distractor for single_choice; flag 'since/rather than/because' riders that appear in the keyed option but no distractor.
